newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products steady in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products steady in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Singapore oil products were steady on Friday in quiet trade due to the holidays in the U.S. but underlying sentiment, especially for gas oil, is firm, traders said on Friday.

Physical gas oil trading was steady with a trader bidding for a 150,000-barrels second half December cargo at $31.70 per barrel, against an offer for 150,000 barrels for mid December loading at $31.80, both fob Singapore.
Strong buying was seen for physical gas oil on a floating basis with at least three cargoes sold this week at between 50 and 60 cents premium to spot Singapore quotes on a fob basis.

December gas oil swaps came under some selling pressure as the market was seen overbought, traders said. It was last quoted at $31.25/$31.35 and was traded down throughout the day from $31.50 to $31.30, brokers said.
But the December/January backwardation came in slightly on expectations of further buying from India which today issued a second buy tender for January cargoes.

Jet fuel was steady on news of recent large purchases from South Korea for December arrival cargoes with at least eight 30,000-tonne lots heard traded so far with the last cargo sold at a $1.70-1.80 premium to Singapor spot quotes, c-and-f basis.

India awarded its sell tender for 50,000 tonnes of Bombay naphtha lifting in Dec to Dutch trader Vitol at Japanese-linked prices due to strong demand from North Asia. A 25,00-tonne cargo of high aromatic naphtha at a discount of $23.10 a tonne below Japanese quotes fob and low aromatic naphtha at a $17.33 discount. India has another low aromatic naphtha cargo on offer from Vizag on the east coast, lifting December 15-17.
Traders the backwardation was under temporary pressure as buyers backed off, expecting prices to fall. At least five more cargoes were sought for Japan in January, traders said.
